To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a power series expansion can be represented by a three-layer feedforward net, that the ordinary delta rule applied to such a net yields a considerable better output error than the backpropagation rule, and that the least squares based simultaneous training rule yields the best approximation results.
the power series network with tSQ-ruie is the fastest network in the class of feedforward neural networks with linear and logarithmic activation functions.
a network based on a power series representation can learn faster and better than a network based on sigmoidal activation functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new neural-net computing techniques, based on power series expansions.
the development of a neural network for power series approximation.
the development and evaluation of a power network for the purpose of power series approximations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power network, trained by tSQ-ru1e, is superior to the sigmoid network trained by backpropagation.
the power series network, trained with the tSQ-rule, is the best of the three methods tested.
power series and neural networks are complementary to each other, in particular with respect to the problem of function approximation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

power networks with linear activation functions in the hidden and output layers, trained by the delta rule or the lSQ-ruie, can be used as a fast, accurate, and reliable tool for power series approximation.
power networks are very fast, and in many cases more precise, than sigmoid networks.
the power series network with the lSQ-ruie is the best choice if one wants to approximate a function by a power series.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power network can be a useful alternative for approximating a wide variety of functions, especially if the number of data points is large.
power series are an efficient representation for neural nets, which is especially true for functions with a large number of terms, such as the inverse of a function.
the performance of power series networks can be significantly improved by using the tSQ- rule.
